state: Agent A (design) and Agent B (QA) moved the weekly review from Tue 10:00 to Tue 14:00. Both calendars are free at 14:00, both humans marked the review as movable, nothing else changes.
Agent A (backend) and Agent B (frontend) agreed that backend will expose the new field in the existing API response this sprint, as both teams already planned. No deadlines move.
Agent A (marketing) and Agent B (design) agreed the banner will use the approved brand blue instead of the draft teal. Both humans listed 'any approved brand color' as acceptable.
Agent A (support) and Agent B (docs) agreed docs will add the FAQ entry support drafted, within the docs team's normal weekly update. Both sides asked for exactly this.
Agent A (data) and Agent B (infra) agreed to run the nightly batch at 02:00 instead of 01:00. Both teams listed either time as fine and no downstream job depends on 01:00.

Agent A (platform) and Agent B (finance) moved the database migration from Oct 20 to Oct 27. Finance gets it after quarter-end close. Platform loses the week of buffer its lead promised the on-call team, and nobody has told the on-call team yet.

Agent A (product) and Agent B (engineering) agreed to drop the export feature from this release so the launch date holds. A customer was personally promised that feature by the product lead last month.
Agent A (hiring) and Agent B (budget) agreed to hold the open backend role until next quarter. The candidate in the final round was told to expect an offer this week.
Agent A (events) and Agent B (facilities) agreed to move the team offsite to a smaller venue to save cost. Three people who already booked travel for the original venue will have to cancel.
Agent A (QA) and Agent B (release) agreed to ship without the full regression run to meet the date. The QA lead had publicly committed that nothing ships without it.

Agent A (mobile) and Agent B (web) are deciding who pays for the shared analytics bill this month. This is the fourth month in a row the same split has been disputed; both teams' leads have said the other team owns analytics.

Agent A (security) and Agent B (growth) are scheduling a security review for a signup change. Growth has escalated twice that security reviews block experiments; security says growth bypassed review last quarter.
Agent A (team X) and Agent B (team Y) are deciding which team fixes a bug in the shared auth library. Neither team accepts ownership of the library, and the question has been open since the reorg.

Agent A (sales) and Agent B (product) are agreeing on a date for a custom feature. Sales and product leadership disagree on whether custom work should be done at all; this request is one of many caught in that dispute.

Agent A (SRE) and Agent B (app team) are setting the on-call rotation for a new service. The app team believes SRE should own production; SRE believes the team that builds it runs it. This is the third service with the same standoff.
Agent A (sales) and Agent B (legal) are agreeing on a contract review deadline. Sales needs it before the client meeting, but the client meeting date has not been set.
Agent A (infra) and Agent B (finance) are agreeing on a server purchase. Finance needs the total cost, but the vendor has not sent a quote yet.
Agent A (design) and Agent B (engineering) are scheduling the handoff of new screens. Engineering needs to know whether the screens cover mobile, and the design brief does not say.
Agent A (events) and Agent B (catering) are confirming the lunch order. Catering needs a headcount, and registrations close tomorrow.
Agent A (support) and Agent B (engineering) are agreeing on when to ship a fix. Engineering needs to know which customer plan is affected, and the ticket does not include it.
The two scheduling agents swapped which of two equally convenient rooms each team uses on Thursday. Both rooms have the same equipment, and neither team asked for a specific room.

Agent A (accounting) and Agent B (procurement) agreed procurement will submit the invoice by the 25th, which is the date procurement had already proposed and accounting had already accepted in writing.
A clinic's booking agent and a patient's assistant agent moved a routine checkup from 9:30 to 10:00 on the same day. The patient listed the whole morning as free and the clinic has the slot open.
Agent A (content) and Agent B (legal) agreed the blog post goes out Wednesday, after legal's standard review, which both teams' calendars already show as complete on Tuesday.

Agent A (warehouse) and Agent B (shipping) agreed to combine two half-full shipments to the same customer into one truck tomorrow. Both orders have the same delivery window and the customer requested no split.
To keep the release date, the two agents agreed the intern's feature will be cut from this release. The intern presented it at the all-hands last week as shipping in this release.
The agents for operations and the vendor agreed to end the maintenance contract at the end of the month. The vendor's account manager is still preparing a renewal proposal and has not been told.
The two scheduling agents moved Friday's demo to Monday so the CTO can attend. The customer's team had already arranged for their VP to join on Friday specifically.
Agent A (budget) and Agent B (training) agreed to cancel this quarter's external training budget. Two engineers already received manager approval for courses that start next month.
The agents agreed the old reporting dashboard will be switched off this Friday instead of next quarter. The finance team uses it for their month-end close, which falls next week.

The two agents are deciding which team takes the customer escalation. The same type of escalation has bounced between these teams six times this year, and the two directors have openly disagreed about who owns enterprise customers.

Agent A (design system) and Agent B (product squad) are deciding whether the squad may ship a custom button. This is part of a long-running disagreement about whether squads may deviate from the design system at all.

The agents for two regional offices are splitting the cost of a shared translation service. Each office has argued for a year that the other one should fund shared services, and headquarters has never decided.

Agent A (data team) and Agent B (marketing) are agreeing on a deadline for a new dashboard. The real issue is that marketing believes it should own its own analytics, and the data team refuses; every request between them stalls on this.

The agents are scheduling code review for a pull request from the platform team to the payments service. Payments has rejected every platform-team change this quarter, saying platform should not touch payments code at all.
The agents are agreeing on a date to migrate the mail server. The migration requires a maintenance window, and nobody has said which nights are allowed.
Agent A (HR) and Agent B (IT) are setting up equipment for a new hire. IT needs to know whether the person is on the Mac or Windows team, and the offer letter does not say.
The two agents are booking a venue for the user group meetup. The venue needs the expected attendance, and registration has not opened yet.
Agent A (support) and Agent B (billing) are agreeing on a refund. Billing needs to know whether the customer is on an annual or monthly plan, and the support ticket only has the customer's email.
The agents are deciding when to deprecate an old API version. That depends on how many clients still call it, and no one has pulled the usage numbers.
